newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak PM sees little chance of NATO inclusion.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM sees little chance of NATO inclusion.

text.p: Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said on Tuesday his country had little chance of being included in the first wave of NATO's eastward enlargement given the negative attitude of the United States toward Slovakia.

Slovakia has often said it wanted to be among the first group of new members to join the alliance, but its chances appear to have waned in recent months after repeated U.S. and European Union criticism of the pace of its democratic reforms.

"With regard to the negative attitude of the U.S., it makes it very unlikely that Slovakia will be in the first wave of NATO applicants," Meciar told journalists at a joint news conference with visiting Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

Chernomyrdin, on the second day of a three-day official visit to Bratislava, said Russia remained steadfastly opposed to the expansion of the alliance, and that he did not want it to become a dominant subject in Russian-Slovak relations.
When asked if Russia would prefer Slovak neutrality, Chernomyrdin said: "From what I have said it means that we would support any solutions oriented this way."

Moscow, which opposes the expansion, has demanded the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation should not station nuclear and other weapons in new member states and wants a binding treaty on relations between Russia and the alliance.

NATO is to decide on which members it will invite to join the security alliance when it meets in Madrid in July. The Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary are considered leading candidates for admittance.
